title: Interval fields: whole numbers within exact caps
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as an Owner/Admin (Settings Service), on the build under test. The Maintenance Reminders feature is on (behind the maintenance_reminders flag). These are numeric/date-accuracy cases (Rule 116): seed the exact inputs, read the produced value back, and compare it to the stated value - never eyeball, never accept "a number".
  2. A routine service form with calendar (days/months), distance and engine-hours interval rows visible (Add service, tick Distance and Engine hours). Know each cap before testing.
custom_steps:
1. In the mileage interval enter 999,999, then 1,000,000.
  2. In the engine-hours interval enter 99,999, then 100,000.
  3. In a days interval enter 999, then 1,000.
  4. Read the calendar months list and try 1 and 12.
  5. Enter 0, a decimal, and a negative in any interval; try to type letters and symbols.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Interval values are whole numbers, minimum 1: mileage caps at 999,999 (1,000,000 refused), engine hours at 99,999 (100,000 refused), days at 999 (1,000 refused); calendar months run 1-12.
  • 0, a decimal and a negative are each refused inline; a number field accepts digits only, so letters and symbols do not enter and there is no error to show.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780; story SV-10559 (S2); Chunk 1 MR spec (Confluence 886931488), S2; read 29 Sep 2026. Source-verified 29 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R9: “Interval values are whole numbers, minimum 1, with no decimals and no negatives. Mileage is capped at 999,999, engine hours at 99,999 and days at 999. An interval longer than 12 months is set in days”
